facets.q: Which NDT method should a Denver candidate certify in first?
facets.a: Ultrasonic testing. It is the only method that pays across both halves of the Front Range market — UT thickness and phased array at Suncor Commerce City and on DJ Basin pipe, UT of bondlines and machined structure at the space primes. SNT-TC-1A recommends 40 hours of formal UT training and 630 method hours plus 1,200 total NDT hours at Level II, so start the experience clock immediately.

facets.q: Does an ASNT NDT Level II certificate satisfy a Colorado aerospace employer?
facets.a: No, not on its own. NAS 410 requires examination on aerospace hardware and a NANDTB-graded Level III, and ASNT certification is not accepted as meeting those requirements beyond the general examination. An ASNT Level II proves method knowledge and shortens your onboarding at Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems or Sierra Space, but the employer still qualifies you against its own NAS 410 written practice.

facets.q: Where do Denver candidates sit ASNT computer-based examinations?
facets.a: At any Pearson VUE test centre in the metro, which covers the 50-question general and 40-question specific written examinations for ASNT NDT Level II. Colorado has no ASNT Authorized Exam Center. The three AECs are Houston, Marietta in Georgia, and Saudi Arabia, and ASNT's Houston facility at 912 Gemini Street is the only site delivering hands-on practicals alongside computer-based tests.

facets.q: How many training hours does SNT-TC-1A recommend for UT Level II?
facets.a: Forty hours of formal training at Level I and a further 40 at Level II, backed by 210 method hours and 400 total NDT hours for Level I, rising to 630 method hours and 1,200 total NDT hours for Level II. Radiography carries the same 40-plus-40 training profile. Magnetic particle is 12 then 8 hours; penetrant is 4 then 8; visual is 8 then 16.

facets.q: What does the Suncor Commerce City refinery add to Denver NDT demand?
facets.a: It is Colorado's only refinery, running roughly 98,000 barrels per day, and it is the single largest concentrated source of fixed-equipment inspection work in the state. Suncor scheduled routine maintenance and upgrade work at the site in March 2026. Turnaround and outage windows there create short, intense hiring bursts for UT thickness, phased array and weld radiography technicians.

facets.q: Is online NDT training accepted on the Front Range?
facets.a: Theory delivered online is accepted for the classroom hours in a written practice. Practical hours are not. SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 both require demonstrated hands-on capability, and ASNT places responsibility for visual acuity, practical and job-specific examinations on the employer. A hybrid route — online theory, in-person lab and practical — is the format that clears an audit.

sections.heading: Two certification systems share one metro, and they do not talk to each other
paragraphs: The mistake that costs Denver candidates a year is treating "NDT training" as one product. It is two. NAS 410 governs who may perform, interpret and accept NDT on aircraft, spacecraft, missiles and engine components. SNT-TC-1A governs pressure equipment, pipelines, structural steel and refining. NAS 410 says "shall" throughout — nothing in it is optional. SNT-TC-1A says "should", and the employer selects, modifies and documents what it will enforce inside its own written practice.

The consequence is practical. A technician qualified to a refinery written practice who applies to a space prime does not arrive with transferable Level II status. NAS 410 imposes tighter vision requirements, requires examination on aerospace parts rather than generic specimens, mandates NANDTB grading for Level III instead of employer grading, and fixes recertification at five years. The refinery route allows an employer-graded Level III and a three-to-five-year interval the employer sets.

Decide which side of that line your career sits on before you pay for a single hour. If the answer is aerospace, your written practice is the prime's. If the answer is energy or fabrication, start from our [US NDT training programme](/training-usa) and the method sequence below.

sections.heading: The method mix Denver actually buys
paragraphs: Front Range aerospace demand concentrates in surface and volumetric methods suited to castings, forgings, welded assemblies and bonded composite structure. Fluorescent penetrant leads, because it is the workhorse for machined aluminium and titanium parts. Eddy current follows for surface and near-surface cracking on conductive components. Radiography and digital radiography cover castings and closure welds. Ultrasonics covers bondline integrity and thickness on machined structure. Magnetic particle appears where ferromagnetic hardware is in scope, which is a smaller share than it is in refining.

Energy demand on the same corridor inverts that ranking. Suncor Commerce City and the DJ Basin buy ultrasonic thickness on piping circuits and vessels, phased array on welds and corrosion mapping, radiography on girth welds against API 1104 and ASME B31.8 acceptance, and MT and PT as surface confirmation. Visual testing sits underneath all of it and is the cheapest credential to hold.
The overlap between the two lists is ultrasonics and penetrant. That overlap is the reason a Denver candidate who certifies in UT and PT first stays hireable regardless of which employer calls back.

sections.heading: The NAS 410 route, clause by clause
paragraphs: NAS 410 is published by the Aerospace Industries Association and is the personnel standard the US aerospace primes require of anyone performing NDT on flight hardware. Its structure resembles SNT-TC-1A — Level I, II and III, training hours, experience hours, examinations — but the enforcement is different in kind. Requirements are mandatory rather than recommended, and the employer cannot dilute them in a written practice the way SNT-TC-1A permits.

The three provisions that matter most to a Denver candidate are the vision requirements, the aerospace-parts examination requirement and the Level III grading route. NAS 410 vision testing is stricter and repeated more frequently. Practical examinations must use aerospace hardware representative of what you will inspect, so generic weld coupons do not qualify you. Level III candidates must sit examinations graded by a National Aerospace NDT Board, not by an internal Level III.

EN 4179 is the European counterpart and tracks NAS 410 closely, which matters if you intend to work between US and EU programmes. Our [ASNT certification guide](/asnt-certification) explains where ASNT credentials do and do not carry into an aerospace written practice.

sections.heading: The SNT-TC-1A route: Commerce City and the DJ Basin
paragraphs: Suncor Commerce City is Colorado's only refinery, running roughly 98,000 barrels per day, with Suncor's own materials citing up to 103,000. It carried out routine maintenance and upgrade work in March 2026. A single-refinery state means the fixed-equipment inspection market is concentrated: when Commerce City is in a turnaround window, contractor demand for UT thickness and phased array technicians spikes, and when it is not, that demand largely disappears from the metro.

The DJ Basin absorbs the slack. Weld County produces close to 90% of Colorado crude, and the basin is dominated by Chevron, Occidental and Civitas following consolidation — Chevron holds roughly 600,000 net acres in the basin after the PDC Energy acquisition. That work is pipe-centric: girth weld radiography and automated UT during construction, then in-service ultrasonics, MT and in-line inspection support.
Both segments certify personnel under SNT-TC-1A. Read our breakdown of [what SNT-TC-1A actually requires](/compliance/asnt-snt-tc-1a) before you accept an employer's account of it.

sections.heading: Where a Denver candidate sits the examinations
paragraphs: The written examinations are the easy part logistically. ASNT delivers NDT Level II computer-based tests through Pearson VUE, which has test centres across the Denver metro. The general examination is 50 multiple-choice questions in two hours; the method-specific examination is 40 questions in two hours. ASNT's published 2026 fees for the initial general-plus-specific package are $740 for members and $820 for nonmembers, with retakes and industry-sector add-ons at $370 and $410.

Practical examinations are where Colorado has a gap. ASNT recognises three Authorized Exam Centers — Houston, Marietta in Georgia, and one in Saudi Arabia — and its Houston site at 912 Gemini Street is the only location delivering the full suite including hands-on practicals. Nothing equivalent exists in Colorado. Under the ASNT NDT Level II programme, employers carry responsibility for visual acuity, practical and job-specific examinations anyway.
That shifts the burden onto your training provider and your employer. A Denver programme that ends at the written examination leaves you two-thirds certified.

sections.heading: Hours, days and the two counting systems that trip people up
paragraphs: SNT-TC-1A counts in hours. The ASNT NDT Level II certification programme counts in days. They are not the same ledger and mixing them produces applications ASNT rejects. Under SNT-TC-1A, UT Level II wants 40 formal training hours on top of Level I's 40, plus 630 method hours and 1,200 total NDT hours. Radiography mirrors that at 40 and 40. Magnetic particle is 12 hours then 8; penetrant 4 then 8; visual 8 then 16.

The ASNT NDT Level II programme states its training in days: MT three days, PT two, RT twelve, UT twelve, VT four. Its experience requirements run in days too — MT 40 method days against 76 total NDT days, PT 30 against 58, VT 30 against 58, and RT and UT each 120 method days against 229 total.
Track both from day one. Our [method-by-method hours reference](/blog/ndt-training-hours-requirements-by-method) lays out the full grid so you can evidence either system when an auditor asks.

sections.heading: Delivery formats that fit a hundred-mile corridor
paragraphs: The Front Range employer base is strung from Fort Collins through Boulder, Broomfield, Westminster, Denver, Commerce City, Littleton and Louisville. Nobody commutes that corridor daily for a twelve-day radiography course. The formats that survive here are hybrid — theory delivered online and consumed on shift rotation, then a compressed in-person block for laboratory work and practical demonstration.

For employers, the more efficient structure is on-site delivery. Bringing the instructor and the specimens to your facility removes travel entirely, lets the practical examination use your own hardware rather than generic coupons, and produces qualification records tied to the parts your written practice actually covers. That last point matters more under NAS 410 than under SNT-TC-1A, because aerospace practical examinations must use representative aerospace parts.

We run this as [corporate NDT training](/corporate-ndt-training) delivered at your site, in your methods, against your written practice. Affordable, accessible, fully customizable — request a quote and we will scope it against your headcount and method list.

sections.heading: The written practice is the document that makes your certificate real
paragraphs: A Denver employer's written practice is the instrument that converts training hours into a valid certification. It names the standard, the methods in scope, the training and experience hours the employer will enforce, the examination structure, the vision requirements, the recertification interval and the Level III responsible for grading. If it is silent, vague or copied from a template that does not match how the company actually operates, every certificate issued under it is exposed the moment a client audits.

This is the failure we see most often in the Colorado energy and fabrication market: a written practice built for one method scope while the company has since added phased array, or one that specifies a Level III the company no longer employs. Both are findings, and both invalidate personnel records retroactively in the eyes of a client auditor.

We rebuild these from the operating reality up — see [written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) — and provide the named Level III oversight the document requires through [ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services).

sections.heading: A twelve-month sequence for a Denver candidate
paragraphs: Months one to three: certify VT and PT. Visual wants 8 then 16 formal hours under SNT-TC-1A and penetrant 4 then 8, so both are achievable quickly and both appear on aerospace and energy job specifications. This is what makes you employable as a trainee rather than a candidate, and it starts the total-NDT-experience clock that every later method depends on.

Months three to nine: add MT and begin UT. Magnetic particle is 12 then 8 hours and clears fast. Ultrasonics is the long pole — 40 hours at each level, 630 method hours and 1,200 total hours for Level II — so the experience accrual has to run in parallel with paid work, not after it. Take the ASNT general and specific examinations when your hours support the application.

Months nine to twelve: add phased array if you are energy-bound, or eddy current if you are aerospace-bound. Wage expectations for the first credential set are documented in our [NDT Level II salary breakdown](/ndt-level-2-salary), which is US-filtered rather than global.

faq.q: Can I work at Lockheed Martin or Sierra Space with an ASNT NDT Level II?
faq.a: You can be hired with one, but you will be re-qualified under the employer's NAS 410 written practice. NAS 410 requires examination on aerospace hardware and NANDTB-graded Level III oversight, and ASNT certification does not substitute for those beyond the general examination. Treat the ASNT credential as evidence of method competence that shortens onboarding, not as a transferable aerospace qualification.

faq.q: How much do ASNT NDT Level II examinations cost in 2026?
faq.a: ASNT's published 2026 fee table lists the initial general-plus-specific package at $740 for members and $820 for nonmembers, covering MT, PT, RT, UT or VT. Retakes and industry-sector add-ons are listed at $370 for members and $410 for nonmembers. Those are ASNT's fees, separate from training tuition. Certification renewal runs on a five-year cycle.

faq.q: Is there an ASNT Authorized Exam Center in Colorado?
faq.a: No. ASNT recognises three Authorized Exam Centers — Houston, Marietta in Georgia, and one in Saudi Arabia. Written computer-based tests are available at Pearson VUE centres across metro Denver. Practical and visual acuity examinations remain the employer's responsibility under the ASNT NDT Level II programme, so your training provider and employer must supply the specimens and the qualified examiner.

faq.q: Which Denver-area employers hire NDT technicians?
faq.a: Aerospace: Lockheed Martin at Waterton Canyon, BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems across Boulder, Broomfield and Westminster, and Sierra Space in Louisville. Energy: the Suncor Commerce City refinery, plus DJ Basin operators Chevron, Occidental and Civitas in Weld County. Beyond those, third-party inspection contractors staff both segments, and structural fabrication shops across the metro buy UT, MT and VT.

title: NDT Training Atlanta: Part 145 MRO, NAS 410 and Exam Centers
description: Atlanta NDT training follows engines: Delta TechOps MRO work, Plant Vogtle and Bowen, and a Marietta ASNT exam center. Method mix, NAS 410 and delivery formats.
h1: Why Atlanta's NDT Method Mix Is Set by Engine Shops Rather Than Weld Shops
answer: Atlanta's NDT demand is engine-driven. Delta TechOps, the largest airline MRO in North America, runs eddy current, fluorescent penetrant, Barkhausen noise and radiography under FAA repair station DALR026A — so aerospace personnel standards, not weld codes, govern the hiring. Marietta hosts one of only three ASNT Authorized Exam Centers worldwide.
expansion: Most NDT training pages written for a US metro assume a refining or pipeline market and default to weld radiography and UT thickness. Atlanta breaks that assumption. The anchor employer is Delta TechOps, certified as FAA repair station DALR026A and EASA.145.4380, running certified repair station operations in Atlanta and Minneapolis, and it publishes an NDT method set that reads nothing like a refinery's: eddy current, magnetic Barkhausen noise, ultrasound, magnetic particle, fluorescent penetrant, radiography and infrared thermography. Barkhausen noise in particular does not appear in energy-sector written practices at all — it is a grinding-burn and residual-stress method specific to hardened rotating components. Layered above that is Part 145, which regulates the repair station rather than the technician, and imposes a documentation and authorisation regime that sits on top of whatever personnel standard the shop uses. Certify in the wrong direction here and you will be qualified for work Atlanta does not buy much of.

facets.q: What method should an Atlanta NDT candidate certify in first?
facets.a: Eddy current, if aerospace is the target. Atlanta's dominant employer runs ET across engine and airframe work, and ET Level II is the credential that separates candidates in an MRO hiring pool. If you are targeting power generation or fabrication instead, ultrasonics leads, because Plant Vogtle, Plant Bowen and the pressure vessel shops all buy UT thickness and phased array before they buy anything else.

facets.q: Does FAA Part 145 certify NDT technicians?
facets.a: No. Part 145 certifies the repair station as an organisation — Delta TechOps holds FAA certificate DALR026A and EASA.145.4380. The repair station's procedures manual then defines who is authorised to perform and release NDT, drawing on a personnel standard such as NAS 410. Your NDT certificate qualifies you for the method; the repair station's authorisation roster is what lets you sign the work off.

facets.q: Where is the nearest ASNT Authorized Exam Center to Atlanta?
facets.a: Marietta, Georgia — inside the metro. ASNT recognises three Authorized Exam Centers worldwide: Houston, Marietta and one in Saudi Arabia. Marietta is operated by Applied Technical Services, which has run laboratory testing, calibration and NDT from that site since 1967. Written computer-based tests are also available through Pearson VUE, but practical examinations are scheduled directly with the exam centre.

facets.q: How does NAS 410 differ from SNT-TC-1A for an Atlanta MRO job?
facets.a: NAS 410 is mandatory in every clause; SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice the employer tailors. NAS 410 imposes stricter and more frequent vision testing, requires practical examination on aerospace hardware, mandates NANDTB-graded Level III examinations rather than employer grading, and fixes recertification at five years against SNT-TC-1A's employer-set three-to-five-year interval.

facets.q: What NDT work does Plant Vogtle generate?
facets.a: Units 3 and 4 are Westinghouse AP1000 reactors of roughly 1,100 MW each, entering commercial operation on 31 July 2023 and 29 April 2024 and operated by Southern Nuclear. In-service inspection under ASME Section XI drives ultrasonic examination of piping welds, eddy current of steam generator tubing, and surface methods. Site access qualification and site-specific performance demonstration matter as much as the base certificate.

facets.q: Is Barkhausen noise inspection worth certifying in?
facets.a: Only if you are committed to engine work. Delta TechOps lists magnetic Barkhausen noise inspection among its NDT methods, where it detects grinding burn and residual stress changes in hardened steel components. It has almost no market outside aerospace and bearing manufacture. Certify in ET and PT first, then add Barkhausen noise once you are inside an engine shop that uses it.

sections.heading: Atlanta's method mix is set by engines, not pipe
paragraphs: The single largest NDT employer in the metro is an engine shop. Delta TechOps is the largest airline maintenance, repair and overhaul provider in North America, holds FAA repair station certificate DALR026A and EASA.145.4380, and operates certified repair station locations in Atlanta and Minneapolis. Its published NDT method set is eddy current, magnetic Barkhausen noise, ultrasound, magnetic particle, fluorescent penetrant, radiography and infrared thermography.

Read that list against a refinery's and the difference is structural. There is no phased array corrosion mapping on it, no automated UT of girth welds, no tank floor scanning. Instead there is Barkhausen noise — a residual-stress and grinding-burn method for hardened rotating components — and infrared, and a heavy weighting toward eddy current and fluorescent penetrant, which are the two methods that dominate high-volume machined-part inspection.

A candidate who trains for the generic "NDT technician" job description in Atlanta trains for the wrong market. Start with our [US training programme](/training-usa) and choose the aerospace track deliberately rather than by default.

sections.heading: What FAA Part 145 adds on top of an NDT certificate
paragraphs: Part 145 is a regulation about organisations. It certifies the repair station, sets out what ratings it holds, and requires a repair station manual and quality control manual that define processes, records and the authority to approve articles for return to service. It does not certify you. This is the distinction candidates get wrong most often.

In practice this means your NDT certification qualifies you for the method, and the repair station's own procedures then determine whether you are on the authorised personnel roster for that method, on that article type, under that rating. Those procedures reference a personnel standard — NAS 410 for aerospace — and add repair-station-specific requirements on training records, continuation training, technique sheets and record retention.

The consequence for a training decision is that Atlanta MRO employers care intensely about the auditability of your qualification record, not just the certificate on the wall. Hours must be evidenced, the practical must have used representative hardware, and the vision test must be current. A [documented, defensible record](/report-validation) is the thing that survives an FAA or customer audit.

sections.heading: NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A: the fork every Atlanta candidate hits
paragraphs: NAS 410 is published by the Aerospace Industries Association and governs who may perform, interpret and accept NDT on aircraft, spacecraft, missiles and aerospace engine components. Every requirement in it is expressed as "shall". SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice using "should", which the employer selects from and adapts inside its own written practice. That single grammatical difference produces the entire divergence in how the two systems behave.

The four differences that decide an Atlanta career: NAS 410 vision requirements are tighter and tested more frequently; NAS 410 practical examinations must use aerospace parts, so generic weld coupons do not qualify you; NAS 410 Level III examinations must be graded by a National Aerospace NDT Board rather than by an internal Level III; and NAS 410 recertification runs on a fixed five-year cycle against SNT-TC-1A's employer-set three-to-five years.

If you are heading for Delta TechOps or an aerospace supplier, the aerospace route is the only one that counts. If you are heading for Vogtle, Bowen, Scherer or a fabrication shop, work from [what SNT-TC-1A actually requires](/compliance/asnt-snt-tc-1a) and build the hours ledger it demands.

sections.heading: Marietta is one of three ASNT Authorized Exam Centers on earth
paragraphs: ASNT delivers its NDT Level II written examinations as computer-based tests through Pearson VUE, and separately recognises a small number of Authorized Exam Centers. There are three: Houston, Marietta in Georgia, and one in Saudi Arabia. Atlanta candidates therefore have an advantage that Denver, Chicago and Los Angeles candidates do not — an AEC inside their own metro.

Marietta is operated by Applied Technical Services, which has run laboratory testing, calibration, NDT and consulting engineering from that site since 1967 and is recognised by ASNT for computer-based and practical examinations. Written tests are scheduled through the MyCert portal and Pearson VUE; practical examinations are scheduled directly with the centre.

The written examination format is fixed: 50 multiple-choice questions in two hours for the general examination, 40 questions in two hours for the method-specific examination. ASNT's published 2026 fees are $740 for members and $820 for nonmembers for the initial general-plus-specific package, with retakes and industry-sector add-ons at $370 and $410. Employers remain responsible for visual acuity, practical and job-specific examinations.

sections.heading: The power generation lane: Vogtle, Bowen and Scherer
paragraphs: Plant Vogtle brought two Westinghouse AP1000 units online within reach of Atlanta — Unit 3 on 31 July 2023 and Unit 4 on 29 April 2024, at roughly 1,100 MW each, operated by Southern Nuclear on behalf of Georgia Power, Oglethorpe Power, MEAG Power and Dalton Utilities. New nuclear generates a long tail of in-service inspection under ASME Section XI: ultrasonic examination of piping welds, eddy current of steam generator tubing, and surface methods on supports and welded attachments.

The fossil fleet extends that demand rather than replacing it. Georgia Power has moved retirement of Plant Bowen — four coal units capable of 3,376 MW, among the largest coal stations in the world — to 2035, and Plant Scherer Unit 3 to 2038, citing industrial and data centre load growth. Life extension on ageing boilers means more tube thickness surveys, more header examinations, more weld repair verification, not less.

Nuclear work carries an access and qualification layer above the certificate. Site-specific performance demonstration, background clearance and a documented training record all gate entry. Employers running these programmes lean on [ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) to keep procedures and personnel files audit-ready between outages.

sections.heading: Fabrication, automotive and the logistics base
paragraphs: Below the anchor employers sits a broad Georgia manufacturing and fabrication base — pressure vessel shops, structural steel fabricators, automotive and battery plants, and the materials-handling and lifting equipment fleet that a logistics hub of Atlanta's size sustains. This segment buys the conventional code methods: radiography and ultrasonics of welds to AWS D1.1 or ASME Section VIII acceptance, magnetic particle and penetrant for surface confirmation, and visual testing throughout.

Radiography is the bottleneck credential in this lane. Under SNT-TC-1A, RT wants 40 formal training hours at Level I and a further 40 at Level II, and the ASNT NDT Level II programme sets RT at twelve training days with 120 method days against 229 total NDT days — the heaviest experience requirement of any method alongside UT. Shops that cannot staff RT interpretation subcontract it, which is why RT Level II holders stay employed through downturns.
Crane, hoist and lifting equipment inspection is the quietest reliable demand in a logistics metro. It runs on MT, PT, VT and UT of terminations, and it does not follow the aerospace or power cycles.

sections.heading: Delivery formats that work around a shift roster
paragraphs: MRO and generation both run rosters that make a twelve-consecutive-day radiography course impossible for most incumbent staff. The formats that clear in Atlanta are hybrid: theory delivered online and consumed across a rotation, then a compressed in-person block for laboratory work and practical demonstration, scheduled against the shift pattern rather than against a training calendar.

For employers, on-site delivery is materially better than sending people out. The instructor and specimens come to your facility, the practical examination uses your own hardware — which NAS 410 requires anyway — and the resulting qualification records tie directly to the articles in your repair station rating or your written practice scope. It also removes the travel and downtime that makes external courses expensive in ways tuition alone does not capture.

sections.heading: Hours and experience: what you must be able to evidence
paragraphs: Two counting systems run in parallel and Atlanta candidates mix them constantly. SNT-TC-1A counts in hours: UT is 40 formal training hours at Level I and 40 more at Level II, backed by 210 method hours and 400 total NDT hours for Level I rising to 630 method hours and 1,200 total for Level II. RT mirrors UT at 40 and 40. MT is 12 then 8, PT 4 then 8, VT 8 then 16.

The ASNT NDT Level II certification programme counts in days: MT three training days, PT two, RT twelve, UT twelve, VT four. Its experience requirements run in days as well — MT 40 method days against 76 total, PT 30 against 58, VT 30 against 58, and RT and UT each 120 method days against 229 total NDT days.

Record both ledgers from your first paid hour. The [full method-by-method hours grid](/blog/ndt-training-hours-requirements-by-method) sets out what an auditor will ask you to evidence, and in which unit.

sections.heading: The five-year clock and what breaks it
paragraphs: ASNT NDT Level II certification renews on a five-year cycle. NAS 410 fixes recertification at five years as well. SNT-TC-1A leaves the interval to the employer, commonly three to five years, stated in the written practice. Whichever governs you, the clock is the least of the risks — what actually breaks certifications is a lapse in the supporting evidence rather than a missed date.

Three failure modes recur. Vision testing lapses, which invalidates every examination performed after the expiry under a NAS 410 written practice. Method scope drifts, where a shop adopts phased array or digital radiography without amending the written practice or requalifying personnel. And the responsible Level III leaves, which leaves every certificate issued under their signature without a technically accountable owner.

All three are audit findings, and all three are retroactive. Employers who cannot keep a Level III on staff between recruitments use [ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) to hold the accountability without a permanent headcount.

faq.a: Delta TechOps operates FAA repair station DALR026A from Atlanta and runs an NDT method set covering eddy current, Barkhausen noise, ultrasound, magnetic particle, fluorescent penetrant, radiography and infrared. Roles are posted through Delta's own careers channel. Come with ET or PT Level II, a current vision test, and a qualification record whose hours and practical examinations can be evidenced against an aerospace personnel standard.

faq.q: Is an ASNT NDT Level II enough for an Atlanta aerospace job?
faq.a: It gets you interviewed, not authorised. Aerospace employers requalify incoming technicians against their own NAS 410 written practice, which requires practical examination on aerospace hardware and NANDTB-graded Level III oversight. ASNT certification is not accepted as satisfying NAS 410 beyond the general examination. It remains valuable evidence of method knowledge and shortens the internal qualification path considerably.

faq.q: What does ASNT NDT Level II certification cost in 2026?
faq.a: ASNT's published 2026 fee table lists the initial general-plus-specific examination package at $740 for members and $820 for nonmembers across MT, PT, RT, UT and VT. Retakes and industry-sector add-ons are listed at $370 for members and $410 for nonmembers. Those are ASNT's examination fees only, separate from training tuition and from any employer practical examination.

faq.q: Which is the better Atlanta certification path — aerospace or power?

title: NDT Training Houston: Turnaround Timing, PAUT and ASNT Exams
description: Houston NDT training, timed to turnaround season: ASNT's only full-practical exam site is here, UT and PAUT dominate, and spring windows set your deadline.
h1: Timing NDT Certification to Houston's Turnaround Calendar
answer: Houston is the only place on earth where ASNT delivers its full examination suite — hands-on practicals and computer-based tests — at one site, 912 Gemini Street. expansion: Every other US metro treats NDT certification as a calendar-neutral decision. Houston does not. facets.q: Why is Houston the best US city to certify in NDT?
facets.a: Because ASNT put its own facility here. The Houston site at 912 Gemini Street is the only location delivering the full suite of ASNT certification examinations, hands-on practicals and computer-based tests together, covering ASNT NDT Level II and III, ASNT 9712 Level II and III, IRRSP radiation safety and Industry Sector Qualification examinations. facets.q: When should a Houston candidate finish certification?
facets.a: Six to eight weeks before a turnaround window opens. Spring turnarounds run late February through May and fall turnarounds September through November, and contractor crews are selected before the outage begins. Finishing in the middle of a window means waiting for the next one. Work backwards from the window, set the examination date, then build the training and experience evidence to meet it.

facets.q: Which method earns most on the Ship Channel?
facets.a: Phased array ultrasonics, layered on a UT Level II foundation. Conventional UT thickness is the volume work — every piping circuit and every condition monitoring location — but PAUT is what contractors are short of during turnarounds, and shortage sets rate. Add TOFD if you are moving toward fabrication and offshore girth welds rather than in-service corrosion monitoring.

facets.q: Do I need an API certification to work in Houston refineries?
facets.a: Not to perform NDT. API 510, 570 and 653 certify inspectors who evaluate fitness-for-service and authorise repairs — a different role from the technician who acquires the data. NDT technicians are qualified under the employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice. Atlantis does not deliver API certification training; we deliver the ASNT method training beneath it, plus Level III oversight and report validation.

facets.q: How large is the Houston-area refining base?
facets.a: Marathon's Galveston Bay refinery at Texas City runs 631,000 barrels per calendar day, the second-largest in the United States, and ExxonMobil Baytown is among the largest. ExxonMobil scheduled first-quarter 2026 turnaround work on a 108,000 barrel-per-day crude pipe still at Baytown and a 180,000 barrel-per-day crude unit at Beaumont. That density is why the region absorbs more inspection labour than any other in North America.

facets.q: Did the LyondellBasell closure shrink Houston NDT demand?
facets.a: It removed one asset, not the market. LyondellBasell completed the shutdown of its 263,776 barrel-per-day Houston refinery in February 2025 after a ramp-down that began in late January. The company has said it plans to convert existing hydrotreaters on the Ship Channel site for recycled-plastics production after 2027. Decommissioning, mothballing and conversion all generate inspection work of their own.

sections.heading: The exam infrastructure is the reason Houston is different
paragraphs: ASNT operates a facility at 912 Gemini Street in Houston, and describes it as the only location offering the full suite of ASNT certification examinations — hands-on practicals alongside computer-based testing. Onsite examinations there cover ASNT NDT Level II and Level III, ASNT 9712 Level II and Level III, Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel, and Industry Sector Qualification. The site runs instructor-led training in equipped NDT laboratories.

That single fact restructures the certification path for a Houston candidate. Everywhere else, written examinations happen at a Pearson VUE centre and the practical is thrown back onto the employer, who under the ASNT NDT Level II programme is responsible for visual acuity, practical and job-specific examinations. In Houston, the practical and the written can be completed against the same institution in the same trip.

Houston is also one of only three ASNT Authorized Exam Centers worldwide, alongside Marietta in Georgia and one in Saudi Arabia. Start from our [NDT training programme](/training) and treat the local examination access as a scheduling advantage, not an afterthought.

sections.heading: Turnaround season is your certification deadline
paragraphs: Refinery turnarounds cluster into two windows. Spring runs from late February through May, taking the gap after winter heating demand and before summer gasoline demand peaks. Fall runs September through November, after the driving season and before winter heating returns. Refiners avoid taking capacity offline when margins are highest, which is why the calendar is this rigid.

Contractor crews are assembled ahead of those windows, not during them. ExxonMobil scheduled first-quarter 2026 work including a 108,000 barrel-per-day crude pipe still at Baytown and a 180,000 barrel-per-day crude unit at Beaumont, and hiring for scopes of that size closes weeks before the unit comes down. A UT Level II awarded in mid-April is a UT Level II that waits until September.

Work backwards. Pick the window, set the examination date six to eight weeks ahead of it, then reverse-engineer the training block and the experience evidence. Our [US training schedule](/training-usa) is structured around those two windows rather than a generic academic calendar.

sections.heading: UT thickness and PAUT: what the Ship Channel actually pays for
paragraphs: The volume work in Houston is ultrasonic thickness measurement. Every piping circuit carries condition monitoring locations, every pressure vessel carries a thickness survey, and the data feeds the inspection plans that drive repair and replacement decisions. It is the most repeatable, most schedulable, most staffed activity in the region — and it is the entry point.

Phased array is where the shortage sits. PAUT covers weld examination, corrosion mapping and complex geometry that conventional UT handles poorly, and turnaround scopes routinely exceed the available qualified headcount. TOFD sits alongside it for girth welds on fabrication and offshore work. Both are extensions of a UT Level II foundation, not replacements for it, and both require procedure-specific qualification on top of the method certificate.

Radiography still holds ground on new construction and in fabrication shops, and the choice between the two methods on a given weld is a real engineering decision — we set it out in [RT vs UT for weld inspection](/blog/rt-vs-ut-weld-inspection). Under SNT-TC-1A, both RT and UT demand 40 formal training hours at each level, which is why they take longest to staff.

sections.heading: What the 2025 Houston refinery shutdown changed
paragraphs: LyondellBasell completed the shutdown of its 263,776 barrel-per-day Houston refinery in February 2025, after a ramp-down that began in late January and more than 400 layoffs. The plant had operated since 1918 and was among the oldest still running in the United States. The company has indicated it will convert existing hydrotreaters at the Ship Channel site for recycled-plastics production with equipment added after 2027.

The correct read is a shift in work type, not a contraction. Decommissioning, isolation verification, mothballing and eventual conversion all generate their own inspection scopes — integrity assessment of equipment being repurposed, weld quality on new tie-ins, and thorough documentation of what was left in place. Conversion projects are, in inspection terms, new construction on a brownfield site.

Meanwhile the surviving base is enormous. Marathon's Galveston Bay refinery at Texas City runs 631,000 barrels per calendar day, second only to Motiva Port Arthur at roughly 636,000, and ExxonMobil Baytown ranks among the largest in the country. One asset leaving a market of that density does not move the labour requirement.

sections.heading: The API layer that sits above your ASNT certificate
paragraphs: Houston candidates conflate two roles constantly. The NDT technician acquires and interprets data under the employer's written practice, certified to SNT-TC-1A. The API inspector — 510 for pressure vessels, 570 for piping, 653 for above-ground storage tanks — evaluates fitness for service, sets inspection intervals and authorises repair. The API credential does not qualify you to shoot a radiograph, and an ASNT Level II does not qualify you to sign an inspection plan.

The route between them runs through experience, not through a parallel course. API's individual certification programmes require documented inspection experience and are examined in fixed windows through the year. If your objective is the inspector role, take the technician certification first and accumulate the field time the API application requires; the sequence does not work in reverse.

Atlantis does not deliver API 510, 570 or 653 training. What we do deliver is the ASNT method training that sits beneath it — see [ASNT certification](/asnt-certification) — plus the Level III oversight and report validation that make the resulting data usable in an API inspector's fitness-for-service decision.

sections.heading: Who hires, and where the Houston work physically sits
paragraphs: Third-party inspection contractors carry most of the headcount. MISTRAS operates its Gulf Coast regional headquarters in Houston from the Energy Corridor, with radiographic capability including thirteen in-house bullpens capable of shooting through 16-inch steel, a 6 MeV linear accelerator, X-ray, Iridium-192, Cobalt-60 and computed radiography, alongside UT, PT, MT and VT. In June 2026 it expanded that laboratory for aerospace and defence work, adding weld repair and rework qualified to AWS D17.1.

TEAM, Inc. is headquartered at 13131 Dairy Ashford Road in Sugar Land with roughly 5,300 employees, operating an Inspection and Heat Treating segment that provides conventional and non-destructive testing to the process, pipeline and power sectors. Between the large contractors and the owner-operator inspection departments, the Houston market absorbs more NDT labour than any other in North America.

Geography matters for your commute and your credentials. The Ship Channel corridor, Baytown, Deer Park, Pasadena, Texas City and Sugar Land each run their own site safety council orientations. Those clearances gate access independently of your NDT certification.

sections.heading: Delivery formats that survive a turnaround roster
paragraphs: Nobody working a turnaround attends a twelve-day daytime radiography course. The formats that function in Houston are compressed and scheduled into the shoulder periods — December through early February, and June through August — when units are running and crews are back to routine monitoring. Theory delivered online lets incumbent technicians consume the classroom content on rotation; the in-person block then concentrates entirely on laboratory work and practical demonstration.

For contractors and owner-operators, on-site delivery removes the largest hidden cost, which is not tuition but crew downtime and travel. Bringing the instructor and specimens to your facility means the practical examination uses your own equipment and your own weld and corrosion specimens, so the qualification record maps directly onto the scopes in your written practice.

We run this as [corporate training](/corporate-ndt-training) across UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Affordable, accessible, fully customizable — request a quote and we will build the schedule around your turnaround calendar rather than ours.

paragraphs: ASNT's published 2026 fee table lists the initial general-plus-specific examination package for ASNT NDT Level II at $740 for members and $820 for nonmembers, across MT, PT, RT, UT and VT. Retakes and industry-sector add-ons are listed at $370 for members and $410 for nonmembers. sections.heading: A first-year sequence for a Houston candidate
paragraphs: Months one to three, in the winter shoulder period: certify VT and PT. Both clear quickly, both appear on Ship Channel job specifications, and both start the total-NDT-experience clock that ultrasonics later depends on.

Months three to nine: add MT and start UT. Magnetic particle is 12 then 8 formal hours with 210 method hours and 400 total at Level II. Ultrasonics is the long build — 40 hours of training at each level, then 630 method hours and 1,200 total NDT hours for Level II — so accrue the hours on paid thickness work while you study. Sit the ASNT examinations at the Gemini Street facility when the ledger supports the application.

Months nine to twelve: add phased array ahead of a spring window. Then think about the record, not just the certificate: the data you produce has to hold up when a client or regulator reads it, which is what [makes an NDT report defensible](/report-validation/what-makes-an-ndt-report-defensible). title: Phased Array Training: PAUT Level II Hours, Scan Plans and Pay
description: PAUT training beyond conventional UT: focal laws, wedge choice, scan plans, TCG, encoders and S-scan sizing, plus the 80-hour rule and the published pay gap.
h1: What PAUT Level II Training Adds On Top of Conventional Ultrasonic Testing
answer: PAUT training adds the setup skills conventional UT never teaches: focal law calculation, wedge and probe selection, scan plan geometry, encoder calibration, TCG across the aperture, and S-scan interpretation. ASNT specifies 80 hours of Level II phased array instruction on top of UT Level II. Employers expect an unsupervised PAUT Level II to build the scan plan, not just run it.
expansion: The gap that traps most candidates is that PAUT Level II is not a method certification in its own right — it is a technique layered onto ultrasonic testing. Your employer's written practice certifies you in UT; phased array appears as a technique endorsement with its own training hours, its own practical, and its own specific examination. That means the UT Level II prerequisite is not a formality. Beam angle, refraction, DAC construction and thickness-mode calibration all reappear inside the focal law, and a candidate who guessed their way through conventional UT will not survive a sectorial scan where forty-eight angles are alive at once. Before booking a [PAUT Level II course](/paut-level-2-training-course), confirm your written practice actually recognizes the technique endorsement and states the hours — [written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) is where most programs discover theirs is silent on phased array.
source: ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended training hours and the ASNT Education Phased Array Level II course specification (80 hours); scope statements of ASTM E2700, ASTM E2491, ISO 13588 and ISO 18563; ZipRecruiter US wage aggregates for "NDT Level II" (13 February 2026), "Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing" (22 June 2026), "Phased Array Technician" (20 August 2026) and "PAUT Technician" (6 August 2026); Glassdoor US aggregate for ASNT NDT Level III (2026).

facets.q: Do I need UT Level II before starting phased array training?
facets.a: Yes. Phased array is a technique under the ultrasonic method, not a separate method, so your certification reads UT Level II with a phased array endorsement. The focal law is built on the same refraction, velocity and time-of-flight arithmetic taught at conventional UT Level II. Candidates who enter phased array without that foundation can operate the instrument but cannot verify that its depth readings are correct.

facets.q: How many training hours does a PAUT Level II endorsement require?
facets.a: ASNT specifies 80 hours for its Phased Array Level II course, and most US written practices adopt that number for the technique endorsement. It sits on top of the SNT-TC-1A recommendation of 40 hours at UT Level I and 40 hours at UT Level II, giving 160 classroom hours in total. Written practices commonly add three months of documented supervised phased array work before certification is signed.

facets.q: What is the difference between TCG and DAC in phased array?
facets.a: DAC corrects amplitude for attenuation along one fixed angle. A sectorial scan changes angle, metal path and wedge path continuously, so a single curve cannot serve the sweep. Time-corrected gain builds a separate gain-versus-time correction at every angle in the focal law from a reference reflector acquired at several depths. Without it, amplitude falls off at the extremes of the sweep, exactly where the fusion faces are examined.

facets.q: Is an encoder mandatory for phased array weld inspection?
facets.a: Unencoded scanning is legitimate for screening and for locating an indication quickly. Encoded scanning is what produces a re-openable data file with every indication tied to a station along the weld. If the deliverable is a report a third party must audit, or one a repair crew must re-find flaws from months later, the scan needs an encoder and a wheel calibrated against a known distance.

facets.q: How much more does phased array pay than conventional ultrasonic testing?
facets.a: ZipRecruiter put the US average for "Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing" at $87,706 a year on 22 June 2026, against $61,725 for "NDT Level II" on 13 February 2026 — a gap of about 42 percent. The phased array figure sits above the 75th percentile of the general Level II band, which the same source put at $71,500. Certified technique work, not the job title, drives the premium.

facets.q: Can phased array replace radiography on production welds?
facets.a: It does so routinely on carbon steel piping and pressure-boundary welds where the governing code accepts ultrasonic examination in place of radiography for that joint. The operational case is no radiation source, no exclusion zone and no shift shutdown, plus a data file the client can reopen. The technical case rests entirely on a scan plan that proves the coverage a radiograph would have delivered automatically.

sections.heading: Focal laws: the arithmetic that replaces the wedge chart
paragraphs: A focal law is the delay table the instrument applies to each element so the wavefronts from all of them arrive in phase at one point in the part. Change the angle and you change every delay. Change the wedge and you change the entry point, the sound path and the exit point of every element. Conventional UT training hands you a wedge stamped sixty degrees and a chart of skip distances. Phased array training hands you the parameters — element count, pitch, aperture start, angle range and angle step — that generate hundreds of those wedges in software.

The parameters entered wrong most often are wedge velocity, first element height and probe-to-wedge-front distance. All three are printed on the wedge, all three get typed from memory, and all three shift the computed depth of every indication without producing any visible error on screen. A technician who cannot re-derive depth from time-of-flight by hand has no way to catch it. That is the specific reason a UT Level II foundation is a hard prerequisite rather than a recommendation, and why [method training hours by method](/blog/ndt-training-hours-requirements-by-method) are structured the way they are.

Good instruction makes you build a focal law from a blank setup on a calibration block, verify it against a known side-drilled hole at three separate depths, and then deliberately corrupt one parameter to see what the resulting error looks like on screen. If a course only walks you through loading a saved setup file supplied by the instructor, you are being taught to operate one particular instrument rather than to apply the technique.

sections.heading: Wedge and probe selection is a coverage decision, not a catalog pick
paragraphs: Wedge choice is a coverage argument. The wedge natural angle sets the center of your usable sweep, and steering more than roughly twenty degrees either side of it collapses sensitivity. Element pitch sets how far you can steer at all, because a coarse pitch throws grating lobes at high angles. Frequency trades penetration against resolution: 5 MHz for general carbon steel weld work, 7.5 or 10 MHz for thin wall and small-diameter tubing, 2.25 MHz where attenuation or coarse grain structure defeats anything higher.

The decision is driven by the joint, not by what happens to be in the case. A 37.5-degree single-V on 25 mm plate demands a different aperture and angle range than a compound bevel on 12 mm pipe with a counterbore. Training that never puts a weld prep drawing in front of you produces technicians who select probes by habit, and habit is how root coverage disappears on the first job that is not a flat plate butt weld with clear access on both sides.

Standards name the technique for exactly this reason. ASTM E2700, Standard Practice for Contact Ultrasonic Testing of Welds Using Phased Arrays, governs manual and semi-automated contact work. ISO 13588 covers the use of automated phased array technology on welds and defines graded testing levels. ASTM E2491 and ISO 18563 cover how the instrument and array themselves are characterized and verified. Knowing which of the four your client's specification invokes is part of the job, and it changes the setup you are permitted to run.

sections.heading: The scan plan is the deliverable employers actually check
paragraphs: The scan plan is the drawing that proves the weld will be covered before anyone squeezes couplant onto the surface. It shows the joint geometry to scale, the probe and wedge sitting on the surface at the index offset you will actually use, and the beam envelope for the lowest and the highest angle in the sweep, first leg and second leg. Every zone of the bevel — root, fill, cap, and the fusion faces on both sides — has to fall inside a beam at some angle in the law.

This is the single element most conventional UT technicians have never produced, and it is the first thing a reviewer looks for. When a phased array report gets rejected by a third party, coverage is almost always the reason: the scan was run, the data looks clean, and nothing in the file demonstrates that the far fusion face was ever insonified. [What makes an NDT report defensible](/report-validation/what-makes-an-ndt-report-defensible) works through the identical failure from the reviewer's side of the table.

Training should have you draw scan plans by hand before it lets you near software that draws them for you. The hand version forces you to reason about index offset, skip distance, and the difference between what the first leg reaches and what the second leg reaches after the beam has spread and lost amplitude. Software will happily render a beautiful, fully covered plan for a geometry that does not exist on the job.

sections.heading: TCG, not DAC: calibrating amplitude across the whole sweep
paragraphs: Conventional UT compensates for attenuation with a DAC curve built on one angle. Phased array cannot do that, because the metal path, the wedge path and the transmission coefficient at the interface all change as the angle sweeps. Time-corrected gain applies a separate gain-versus-time correction at every angle in the law, built from the same reference reflector acquired at several depths. Done properly, a 3 mm side-drilled hole reads the same amplitude at 45 degrees and at 70 degrees, and at 15 mm deep and 40 mm deep.

Building TCG takes real bench time. You place the block, acquire the reference reflector at each depth in turn, and let the instrument solve the curve across the whole aperture. Skipping depths, or building TCG on a block with a different velocity or surface condition than the component, produces a calibration that silently undersizes flaws at the extremes of the sweep — which is precisely where the fusion faces of a bevel are examined and where lack of fusion lives.

Verification matters as much as construction. Re-checking TCG at shift change, after a temperature swing, and after any wedge change is a procedural requirement in most written practices, and it is the evidence auditors ask to see. If your instruction never covers what a failed verification obliges you to do with the data already acquired that shift, it has skipped the part of the technique that protects both you and your employer.

sections.heading: Encoders turn a scan into evidence
paragraphs: An unencoded phased array scan is a live picture. An encoded one is evidence. The encoder wheel reports position along the weld, the instrument indexes each A-scan to that position, and the resulting file can be reopened months later with every indication tied to a station number that a fitter can find with a tape measure, without the technician who acquired it standing on the job to interpret from memory.

Encoder calibration is a two-minute task that gets skipped and then invalidates a full day of data. You roll the wheel a known distance — 500 mm along a straight edge is the common choice — and correct the counts-per-millimetre until the readout matches. Slip on a wet or scaled surface, a wheel dragging against a weld cap, or a magnetic wheel jumping a tack will stretch or compress the C-scan, and the resulting position error is invisible in an otherwise clean image.

Encoded data is what makes phased array competitive with radiography on a shutdown. The argument is not only that there is no source and no exclusion zone; it is that the client receives a re-interrogable data file rather than a film they cannot revisit. A technician who only ever scans unencoded cannot make that argument to a client, and cannot deliver the record that justifies replacing a radiographic technique with an ultrasonic one.

sections.heading: Reading an S-scan: separating a flaw from geometry
paragraphs: A sectorial scan paints every angle in the sweep as a wedge-shaped image with the part geometry overlaid on it. The first skill is separating real reflectors from geometry: the root bead, the counterbore, a backing bar and the far surface all produce strong, repeatable indications that sit exactly where the overlay says the geometry sits. The second skill is recognising which angle a real indication responds best at, because the answer tells you how the reflector is oriented in the weld.

Lack of fusion on a bevel face responds strongly at the angle normal to that face and falls away sharply on either side of it. Porosity responds weakly across the whole sweep and moves erratically as the probe moves. A crack shows tip diffraction — a second, weaker signal above the corner reflector — and that tip is what you measure height from. Slag gives a broad, ragged response with no tip at all. None of those signatures is available on an A-scan alone.

Sizing is where phased array earns its premium and where it is most often done badly. Amplitude sizing carried over from conventional UT overcalls long, low-amplitude planar flaws and undercalls short, well-oriented ones. Tip diffraction and the 6 dB drop applied along the correct axis are the techniques that hold up under review. Practise on flawed samples with known answers — [PAUT Level II practice questions](/blog/paut-level-2-practice-questions) cover the theory, but sizing skill only comes off blocks.

sections.heading: Prerequisites, hours and experience: the real timeline
paragraphs: The route is UT Level I, then UT Level II, then phased array. SNT-TC-1A recommends 40 hours of formal instruction at UT Level I and a further 40 at Level II, with method experience accumulating alongside. ASNT's own Phased Array Level II course is specified at 80 hours, and most US written practices adopt that figure for the technique endorsement. That is 160 classroom hours before anyone can call you a credentialed PAUT Level II, and the hours have to be documented.

Experience is the longer pole. Written practices commonly require three months of supervised phased array work on top of the underlying UT method experience, and that supervision has to be documented by a Level III certified in ultrasonic testing. Companies with no UT Level III on staff cannot sign the certification at all, which is why a training purchase frequently fails to unblock a program that actually has a certification-authority problem rather than a knowledge problem.

Two details cause most rejected certifications. First, the written practice must name phased array explicitly and state its training hours and experience requirement; a document that says only "UT" does not cover the technique endorsement. Second, the specific examination has to be written against the equipment and procedures the technician will actually use — a generic phased array exam bought off the shelf does not survive a client audit. [Written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) closes both gaps in a single pass.

sections.heading: What a PAUT Level II is expected to do unsupervised
paragraphs: The employer test is not whether you can operate the instrument. It is whether you can walk up to a joint you have never seen, read the weld prep from the drawing or the welding procedure, choose the probe and wedge, build the focal law, produce a scan plan, calibrate TCG and the encoder, acquire the data, and then interpret and report it without a Level III standing behind your shoulder correcting the setup.

That is the entire reason for the pay gap. A conventional UT Level II is paid to execute a technique somebody else designed. A phased array Level II is paid to design the technique on site and defend it to a client inspector who may know the governing standard better than they do. Companies that treat phased array as a button on the machine end up dispatching a Level III to every job, which erases the economics of owning the equipment in the first place.

The functional checklist contractors actually use has four items: build a setup from scratch in under twenty minutes; explain your coverage from the scan plan without notes; produce a report another technician can reproduce from the data file alone; and name the specification clause you are working to. A technician who clears all four moves permanently to the top of the call-out list, and the call-out list is where the money is.

sections.heading: The pay differential, in published numbers
paragraphs: ZipRecruiter's US aggregate for "NDT Level II" stood at $61,725 a year on 13 February 2026, with the 25th percentile at $48,000, the 75th at $71,500 and the 90th at $90,000. Its aggregate for "Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing" stood at $87,706 on 22 June 2026 — about 42 percent above the general Level II figure, and above the 75th percentile of that band entirely. The premium is not a rumour; it is visible in the posting data.

Read title-matched aggregates carefully before quoting them. The same source's "Phased Array Technician" listing averaged $70,578 on 20 August 2026, and its "PAUT Technician" hourly listing averaged $21.53 with a median of $19.71, because those two titles sweep in helper, trainee and assistant postings that are not certified phased array work at all. The distance between $21.53 an hour and $87,706 a year is the distance between a job title and the certification standing behind it.

The differential compounds upward. Glassdoor's US aggregate for ASNT NDT Level III sat at $100,205 a year in 2026, and a UT Level III who is also the phased array authority for a company sits above that, because they own procedure approval as well as interpretation. [NDT Level II salary](/ndt-level-2-salary) and [NDT Level III salary](/ndt-level-3-salary) break the bands out by region and industry. For a scoped cohort on your own instruments and procedures, [request a demo or a quote](/contact).

faq.q: Is PAUT a separate ASNT method or a technique under ultrasonic testing?
faq.a: It is a technique under the ultrasonic method. There is no standalone ASNT phased array method certification; your certificate reads ultrasonic testing, with phased array recorded as a technique endorsement carrying its own training hours, its own practical demonstration and its own specific examination. This matters when you change employers, because the new written practice has to recognise the endorsement before your phased array work is covered.

faq.q: How long does it take to go from UT Level II to working phased array unsupervised?
faq.a: The instruction is 80 hours. The experience most written practices require on top of it is three months of documented supervised phased array work. In practice, technicians who scan daily reach genuine independence — building setups and scan plans without help — around six months in, and technicians who touch the instrument once a month do not reach it at all. Frequency of use matters more than elapsed time.

faq.q: Should I train on the same instrument my employer owns?
faq.a: Train on the technique, verify on the instrument. Focal law construction, TCG, scan plan geometry and sizing transfer across every manufacturer. Menu structure, setup file handling and calibration wizards do not. A course that teaches only one interface leaves you stranded the first time a client supplies different equipment, so the useful sequence is generic technique first, then a short familiarisation on the specific instrument you will carry.

faq.q: Is a practical examination required for a phased array endorsement?
faq.a: Yes, where your employer's written practice follows SNT-TC-1A. The practical requires you to demonstrate the technique on a specimen and report the results, and it is scored alongside a general and a specific written examination. A written practice that omits the practical for phased array is the finding an auditor writes up, which is why the endorsement should be added to the document deliberately rather than assumed under the existing ultrasonic entry.

faq.q: Can Atlantis deliver phased array training on our own equipment and procedures?
faq.a: Yes. On-site delivery uses your instruments, your calibration blocks, your written practice and your job geometries as the worked examples, so exam preparation doubles as a program review. That combination also produces the specific examination and the documented hours your written practice needs. Delivery is affordable, accessible and fully customizable to your shift pattern — request a demo or a quote for a scoped cohort.

title: API 653 Certification: Prerequisites, Exam Structure and Fees
description: Independent guidance on API 653: eligibility by education, the 170-question split exam, the reference set, API's published fees, and the 2026 exam windows.
h1: What the API 653 Exam Actually Tests — and Where NDT Fits In
answer: API 653 certifies you to evaluate aboveground storage tanks, not to run NDT. The exam is 170 questions across a 110-question closed book and a 60-question open book, over 6.5 hours of testing. API charges $1,125 for non-members and $875 for members. Experience runs one to five years depending on your education.
expansion: Atlantis does not deliver API 653 preparation courses, so what follows is independent guidance with nothing to sell you. The certification is administered entirely by API through its Individual Certification Programs; there is no accredited-provider scheme, so no training company can shorten the eligibility or influence the result. What a course buys you is structured exposure to eight API documents plus two ASME Code sections, and that is worth paying for only once you have confirmed you qualify. The exam is scheduled three times a year in fixed windows, and the application deadline sits roughly two months ahead of each one — miss it and the next opportunity is four months away. Where Atlantis does work is the layer underneath: the [ASNT method certifications](/training) your technicians hold, the [Level III oversight](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) that approves their procedures, and the [report validation](/report-validation) a tank inspector relies on when signing off someone else's data.
source: API Individual Certification Programs: the API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector program page (eligibility, exam structure, recertification), the Body of Knowledge for the March, July and November 2026 exams (dated July 2025, replacing March 2025), and the published ICP schedules and fees. All figures are API's own and are attributed as such; no Atlantis pricing appears because Atlantis does not sell API 653 training.
